---
title: "Data strategy"
---

## Why three tiers {#sec-data-strategy}

The data does not fit. A single imaging run is gigabytes; a high-resolution section is
larger. It cannot be committed, cannot be executed in CI, and cannot be downloaded before
lesson one. This was decided before any lesson was written.

## Three tiers

### Committed toy

**under 10 MB**, in the repository.

Mechanics: the object model, the API, the plot call

*Rule that keeps it honest.* Small enough that lesson one needs no download.

### Fetched public

**0.1 to 10 GB**, fetch script pinned to an accession, cached locally.

The real analysis on real tissue, at real scale

*Rule that keeps it honest.* Never committed. Checksum, provenance and licence recorded per dataset. No patient data, and nothing re-identifiable from tissue morphology.

### Simulated

**tiny**, generator script in the repository.

Ground truth — the only tier where the right answer is known

*Rule that keeps it honest.* The most pedagogically valuable tier and the one most often skipped. It is the only place a reader can measure how far their answer landed from the truth.

## Rules

- Never commit primary data. Commit the script that fetches it, pinned to a specific
  version or accession, and record the checksum.
- Record provenance and licence per dataset in `data/SOURCES.md`. Vendor demo data,
  consortium data and paper supplements have different terms.
- Never use patient data in teaching material, and never data that could be
  re-identified from tissue morphology.
- The simulated tier is the most pedagogically valuable and the most often skipped. It is
  the only place a reader can measure how far their answer landed from the truth.
